title: Cut USAID back to at least its 2019 budget level
proposal: The text recommends shrinking USAID's global footprint by, at a minimum, returning to its 2019 budget level from before the COVID-19 pandemic.
quote: by, at a minimum, returning to the agency’s 2019 pre–COVID-19 pandemic budget level

title: Make deep cuts in the international affairs budget
proposal: The text recommends working with Congress to make deep cuts to the international affairs "150 Account" while giving USAID more flexibility in how it spends its funds.
quote: This will require working closely with the U.S. Congress to make deep cuts in the

title: Make the USAID chief Director of Foreign Assistance over all aid
proposal: The text recommends authorizing the USAID Administrator to also serve as Director of Foreign Assistance, at Deputy Secretary of State rank, in charge of all U.S. foreign aid.
quote: The USAID Administrator should be authorized to take on the additional role of Director of Foreign Assistance (DFA) with the rank of Deputy Secretary

title: Restore USAID's counter-China programs
proposal: The text recommends restoring the Trump-era counter-China structure at USAID, judging aid through a national security lens and rewarding countries that resist China's lending.
quote: The next conservative Administration should restore and build on the Trump Administration’s counter-China infrastructure at USAID

title: Cut off aid partners that deal with Chinese entities
proposal: The text recommends funding programs that counter China in key countries and ending funding to any partner that works with Chinese entities directly or indirectly.
quote: eliminate funding to any partner that engages with Chinese entities directly or indirectly

title: Focus USAID's Asia regional mission on countering China
proposal: The text recommends that USAID's regional mission in Bangkok focus on cross-border projects to counter Chinese influence.
quote: USAID’s Bangkok-based Regional Development Mission for Asia should focus its strategic attention on supporting cross-border initiatives

title: Rescind all climate policies in foreign aid
proposal: The text recommends removing all climate policies from foreign aid programs, specifically USAID's Climate Strategy 2022-2030, and narrowly limiting funding to traditional climate efforts.
quote: The next conservative Administration should rescind all climate policies from its foreign aid programs

title: Close USAID offices that advance the Paris Climate Agreement
proposal: The text recommends shutting down USAID offices, programs and directives designed to advance the Paris Climate Agreement.
quote: shut down the agency’s offices, programs, and directives designed to advance the Paris Climate Agreement

title: Support oil and gas development in poor countries
proposal: The text recommends that USAID stop opposing fossil fuels in developing countries and instead support responsible management of their oil and gas reserves.
quote: USAID should cease its war on fossil fuels in the developing world and support the responsible management of oil and gas reserves

title: Stop funding groups that advocate on climate
proposal: The text recommends that USAID stop working with and funding foundations, companies, international groups and NGOs that it says advocate for "climate fanaticism."
quote: The agency should cease collaborating with and funding progressive foundations, corporations, international institutions, and NGOs that

title: Eliminate USAID's diversity officer, DEI advisers and scorecards
proposal: The text recommends dismantling USAID's diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) structure, including the Chief Diversity Officer job, DEI advisers and committees, and the DEI scorecard and dashboard.
quote: dismantle USAID’s DEI apparatus by eliminating the Chief Diversity Officer position along with the DEI advisers and committees

title: Remove DEI requirements from USAID contracts and grants
proposal: The text recommends removing DEI requirements from USAID contract and grant competitions and awards.
quote: remove DEI requirements from contract and grant tenders and awards

title: Order USAID to stop promoting DEI and LGBTQ+ agendas
proposal: The text recommends a directive telling USAID to stop promoting the DEI agenda, including what it calls the LGBTQ+ agenda.
quote: issue a directive to cease promotion of the DEI agenda, including the bullying LGBTQ+ agenda

title: Create a confidential channel for claims of political retaliation
proposal: The text recommends giving staff a confidential way to bring cases of political retaliation they say they suffered during the Biden Administration.
quote: provide staff a confidential medium through which to adjudicate cases of political retaliation

title: Defund and debar partners that promote DEI practices
proposal: The text recommends ending funding for partners that promote what it calls discriminatory DEI practices and considering debarment in serious cases.
quote: It should eliminate funding for partners that promote discriminatory DEI practices and consider debarment in egregious cases.

title: Dismiss staff and grantees who agitate for DEI
proposal: The text recommends dismissing staff, implementers and grantees who engage in "ideological agitation" for DEI, and debarring such entities.
quote: as well as implementers and grantees that engage in ideological agitation on behalf of the DEI agenda should be dismissed

title: Return civil rights authority to USAID's Office of Civil Rights
proposal: The text recommends putting all civil rights issues at USAID back under the agency's Office of Civil Rights.
quote: should return the authority over all civil rights issues at USAID to the agency’s Office of Civil Rights

title: Rename USAID's gender office as Office of Women, Children, and Families
proposal: The text recommends renaming the Office of Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment, moving its resources, and making its head a pro-life political appointee.
quote: rename the USAID Office of Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment (GEWE) as the USAID Office of Women, Children, and Families

title: Eliminate USAID's 180-plus gender advisors
proposal: The text recommends eliminating the more than 180 gender advisors and contacts placed in USAID missions and units.
quote: eliminate the “more than 180 gender advisors and points of contact

title: Rescind USAID's 2022 Gender Policy
proposal: The text recommends canceling President Biden's 2022 Gender Policy, refocusing it on women, children and families, and revising the related program regulation.
quote: rescind President Biden’s 2022 Gender Policy and refocus it on Women, Children, and Families

title: Remove 'gender' and abortion terms from USAID materials and contracts
proposal: The text recommends removing terms like "gender equality" and "gender equity," and references to abortion and reproductive health, from USAID websites, publications, policies, contracts and grants.
quote: on USAID websites, in agency publications and policies, and in all agency contracts and grants that include the following terms

title: Implement the Geneva Consensus Declaration and favor faith-based partners
proposal: The text recommends that the new Office of Women, Children, and Families implement the Geneva Consensus Declaration and prioritize partnerships with local and faith-based organizations.
quote: prioritize partnerships with local organizations, including faith-based organizations (FBOs)

title: Reinstate and expand the Mexico City Policy to all foreign aid
proposal: The text recommends an executive order restoring the Protecting Life in Global Health Assistance policy (the Mexico City Policy) and applying it to all foreign assistance, including humanitarian aid.
quote: The executive order to reinstate PLGHA should be drafted broadly to apply to all foreign assistance.

title: Block U.S. funding to the U.N. Population Fund
proposal: The text recommends that the same executive order immediately block funding to the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).
quote: should issue an executive order that, at a minimum, reinstates PLGHA and summarily blocks funding to UNFPA

title: Rescind Biden's 'Protecting Women's Health at Home and Abroad' memo
proposal: The text recommends canceling President Biden's January 28, 2021, memorandum that reversed the Mexico City Policy.
quote: It should simultaneously rescind President Biden’s memorandum entitled “Protecting Women’s Health at Home and Abroad,”

title: End Mexico City Policy exemptions for U.S. NGOs and international groups
proposal: The text recommends applying the pro-life policy to subgrantees and removing exemptions for U.S.-based NGOs, public international organizations and government-to-government agreements.
quote: remove exemptions for U.S.-based NGOs, public international organizations, and bilateral government-to-government agreements

title: Require compliance reports and debarment for pro-life policy violations
proposal: The text recommends that all USAID-funded groups report compliance with the pro-life policy, with penalties including debarment, and that USAID publish implementation reports.
quote: USAID should institute penalties, including debarment from future federal funding, for violations of it

title: Keep applying the Helms Amendment ban on funding abortions abroad
proposal: The text recommends continuing to apply the Helms Amendment as a complete ban on using taxpayer money to pay for abortions overseas.
quote: the Helms Amendment should continue to be applied, as it has been by both Republican and Democratic Administrations for more than 50 years

title: Train USAID staff on religious freedom and build it into programs
proposal: The text recommends training all USAID staff on religious freedom and development and building it into all programs, including 2025 country strategies.
quote: It should train all USAID staff on the connection between religious freedom and development

title: Fund aid for persecuted religious minorities
proposal: The text recommends that Congress give USAID funding specifically to support persecuted religious minorities, in line with Executive Order 13926.
quote: Congress should appropriate funding to USAID specifically to support persecuted religious

title: Add pro-life and accountability terms to all USAID awards
proposal: The text recommends making key policy language, including the pro-life policy and conditions on multilateral funding, standard in all USAID grants, cooperative agreements and contracts.
quote: should immediately implement language on key policy topics as standard provisions in all grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts

title: Put a political appointee in charge of USAID procurement
proposal: The text recommends naming a political appointee as USAID's Senior Procurement Executive and head of its acquisition office, placing other appointees there, and changing the Competition Advocate.
quote: the next conservative Administration should name a political appointee as the agency’s Senior Procurement Executive

title: Increase transparency of USAID subawards
proposal: The text recommends letting the Administrator decide the size and scope of awards and making subawards more transparent and accountable.
quote: increase the transparency and accountability of subawards

title: Hire more USAID contracting officers using program funds
proposal: The text recommends using program funds to hire more contracting and agreement officers so disaster funds reach a wider range of implementers faster.
quote: USAID should use existing authority to use program funds to expand its roster of contracting and agreement officers

title: Restore political review of large USAID awards
proposal: The text recommends restoring the Senior Official Accountability Review, or a similar process, so policymakers review proposed programs above a set dollar amount.
quote: or create a similar process to ensure that proposed programs above a certain dollar threshold

title: Shift aid funding to local partners across USAID, following PEPFAR
proposal: The text recommends copying PEPFAR's shift to local partners across all of USAID, including all global health and humanitarian aid, while ramping down large U.N., NGO and contractor partnerships.
quote: This model should be replicated across all of USAID.

title: Expand the New Partnership Initiative and set local-partner quotas
proposal: The text recommends expanding the New Partnership Initiative to every bureau and requiring each mission to send a minimum share of funds to new, underused and local partners.
quote: expand use of the New Partnership Initiative (NPI) to every bureau and office

title: Eliminate cost-plus contracts that favor large aid companies
proposal: The text recommends more open competition and fixed-amount awards and ending cost-plus reimbursement contracts that it says favor large companies.
quote: along with eliminating cost-plus reimbursement contracts that favor large companies

title: Check existing local efforts before starting new USAID programs
proposal: The text recommends requiring USAID to assess existing local activities before launching a new program, to avoid duplicating or undercutting them.
quote: Before advancing a new program, the agency should be required to assess existing local activities to avoid undercutting or duplicating them.

title: Review and update USAID's global health portfolio
proposal: The text recommends updating the Global Health Bureau's portfolio, focusing on women, children and families and local and faith-based partners, and cutting outdated programs.
quote: A rigorous review is necessary to ensure that current programs and funding streams avoid wasting taxpayer dollars

title: Launch a 'Resilient Families' global health funding call
proposal: The text recommends a "Request for Application for Resilient Families" that pools funds from separate programs to focus on individuals and families rather than single diseases.
quote: The Bureau should implement a “Request for Application for Resilient Families”

title: Move PEPFAR and malaria programs toward country ownership
proposal: The text recommends that PEPFAR and the President's Malaria Initiative become part of sustainable health systems in developing countries, moving toward national ownership and funding.
quote: It is time for these programs to become part of an integrated, strong, and sustainable network of health care and public health in developing countries.

title: Apply PEPFAR's data reforms to all global health programs
proposal: The text recommends extending Trump-era PEPFAR data collection and reporting updates to all USAID global health programs.
quote: The next conservative Administration should apply these reforms to all of USAID’s global health programs.

title: Expand private and faith-based health partnerships via USAID's innovation center
proposal: The text recommends empowering the Global Health Bureau's Center for Innovation and Impact to expand networks of private and faith-based health groups using tools like impact bonds.
quote: should be empowered to expand networks of private and faith-based health organizations

title: Reduce the share of contractors in USAID's health bureau
proposal: The text recommends lowering the high ratio of contractors to direct hires in the Global Health Bureau and holding career leaders accountable.
quote: modifying the high ratio of contractors to direct hires

title: Name an appointee to hold the U.N. and WHO accountable
proposal: The text recommends a political appointee to coordinate efforts to hold the U.N., WHO and other partners financially accountable, including removing abortion-promoting language from U.N. documents.
quote: Leadership should designate a political appointee to help coordinate cross-agency efforts to hold the U.S. government’s multilateral partners

title: Deeply cut disaster aid and end programs in Yemen, Syria and Afghanistan
proposal: The text recommends working with Congress to deeply cut the International Disaster Assistance budget by ending programs in places controlled by "malign actors," such as Yemen, Syria and Afghanistan.
quote: Work with Congress to make deep cuts in the IDA budget by ending programs that do more harm than good in places controlled by malign actors

title: Set time limits and exit plans for humanitarian aid
proposal: The text recommends requiring USAID and State to create country exit strategies that limit how long humanitarian responses last and shift funds to development.
quote: devise country-based exit strategies that term-limit the duration of humanitarian responses

title: Shift humanitarian awards from U.N. agencies to local groups
proposal: The text recommends moving away from large awards to U.N. agencies, global NGOs and contractors toward local, especially faith-based, organizations.
quote: Transition from large awards to expensive, inefficient, and corrupt U.N. agencies, global NGOs, and contractors to local, especially faith-based, entities

title: Require USAID's humanitarian bureau to use flexible award rules
proposal: The text recommends that the Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance use existing authorities to drop cost-reimbursement rules that exclude small local NGOs and expand fixed-amount awards.
quote: Require that BHA avail itself of existing IDA authorities that it fails to use

title: Hire more procurement officers for humanitarian aid
proposal: The text recommends that USAID's management bureau hire more procurement officers for the humanitarian bureau, which it says would reduce reliance on large awards.
quote: Direct USAID’s Bureau for Management to hire more procurement officers for BHA

title: Let the humanitarian bureau manage its own contractor hiring
proposal: The text recommends allowing the Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance to manage hiring of Personal Services Contractors.
quote: Allow BHA to manage the process of hiring Personal Services Contractors.

title: Require stricter vetting to keep aid from terrorists
proposal: The text recommends requiring humanitarian aid partners to adopt stricter vetting to prevent aid from being diverted to terrorists.
quote: Require BHA’s partners to adopt stricter vetting procedures to prevent aid from being diverted to terrorists.

title: Condition U.S. humanitarian aid on other donors paying their share
proposal: The text recommends pressing other donors for real contributions, not just pledges, and making that a condition for additional U.S. aid.
quote: Increase efforts to obtain greater contributions, not just pledges, for humanitarian operations from other donors and make this a condition

title: Share a development chief between USAID and the DFC
proposal: The text recommends having the Development Finance Corporation's chief development officer also serve at USAID to better align the two.
quote: The easiest way to foster this alignment is to “dual hat” the role of DFC’s chief development officer

title: Refocus the Development Finance Corporation away from climate goals
proposal: The text recommends returning the DFC to its original commercial risk-reducing role and away from climate, diversity and gender-based activities.
quote: DFC should be restored to its original intent of deploying its commercial risk-reducing financial services

title: Enforce 'from the American people' branding on all aid
proposal: The text recommends building on the Trump-era branding policy so aid partners fully credit the American people, enforced by a political appointee on every award.
quote: to force the aid bureaucracy to fully credit the American people for the aid they are providing

title: Speed up aid spending by cutting budget paperwork
proposal: The text recommends shifting foreign assistance staff to spending already-approved funds, eliminating duplicate resource requests, and sending a required report to Congress within 60 days.
quote: This should include eliminating the duplicative Mission and Bureau Resource Requests

title: Put a political appointee in charge of USAID personnel
proposal: The text recommends quickly naming a political appointee as USAID's Chief Human Capital Officer and exploring hiring under Administratively Determined and Schedule C authorities.
quote: the next conservative Administration should name a political appointee as USAID’s Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO)

title: Pilot Schedule F hiring at USAID
proposal: The text recommends that USAID be one of the first agencies to test a reinstated Executive Order 13957, which created Schedule F, a job category with fewer firing protections.
quote: USAID should be one of the agencies to pilot-test a reinstated Executive Order 13957

title: Recruit veterans and others into term-limited Schedule A jobs
proposal: The text recommends aggressively recruiting veterans and others into term-limited Schedule A positions, and creating a recruiting program for veterans, missionaries and faith community members.
quote: recruit and place candidates into term-limited positions under Schedule A of the Excepted Service (especially veterans)

title: Rotate USAID's senior executives through an SES mobility program
proposal: The text recommends reviewing how senior executives are placed and creating a program to regularly rotate senior career leaders, including to other agencies.
quote: should institute an SES Mobility Program to encourage the regular rotation of senior career leaders

title: Move USAID policy functions under appointees in the Administrator's office
proposal: The text recommends moving the Bureau for Policy, Planning, and Learning's policy work into a renamed budget office in the Administrator's office, staffed by political appointees.
quote: shift the policy functions of the Bureau for Policy, Planning, and Learning (PPL) to the Office of Budget and Resource Management (BRM)

title: Freeze and review all major USAID policies in year one
proposal: The text recommends an immediate freeze on changes to USAID's policy manual and reviewing, amending or withdrawing all major policies within the first year.
quote: All major agency policies should be reviewed and amended or withdrawn within the new Administration’s first calendar year in office.

title: Edit USAID websites and social media to match new policies
proposal: The text recommends reviewing USAID's public web pages and social media to remove material that does not match the new administration's policies.
quote: review and editing of the agency’s public-facing web pages and social media accounts to eliminate material that does not conform

title: Publish all USAID congressional notifications and reports
proposal: The text recommends speeding review of Congressional Notifications and publishing all of them along with congressional reports.
quote: Notifications within LPA and publish all CNs and congressional reports.

title: Centralize USAID communications staff under one bureau
proposal: The text recommends giving the Bureau for Legislative and Public Affairs direct authority over communications staff across USAID and expanding outreach to conservative allies.
quote: LPA should gain direct authority over the communications staff scattered through USAID’s various Bureaus and Offices

title: Appoint political attorneys and clarify faith-based groups' eligibility
proposal: The text recommends appointing Schedule C attorneys (at least four besides the General Counsel) and issuing quick guidance on faith-based groups' eligibility for USAID funding.
quote: OGC should issue clear guidance on the eligibility of faith-based organizations for USAID funding

title: Reprogram already-approved USAID funds to new priorities
proposal: The text recommends that USAID's budget office find already-appropriated funds to redirect immediately to the new administration's priorities.
quote: identify already appropriated resources to reprogram immediately to fund the new Administration’s priorities

title: Redirect USAID democracy bureau funds to new priorities
proposal: The text recommends staffing DDI with appointees, rewriting its policies, and using its central funds for faith-based, minority and private-sector projects, with awards limited to new partners.
quote: harvest DDI’s central appropriations to fund new priorities

title: Deepen aid ties with Japan, Australia, South Korea, India and Taiwan
proposal: The text recommends intensifying development partnerships with Japan, Australia, South Korea and India, and expanding development cooperation with Taiwan.
quote: USAID should intensify its bilateral relationships with pro–free market Japan, Australia, South Korea, and India

title: Target aid to Pacific island states to counter China
proposal: The text recommends targeted aid with allied donors, such as help fighting illegal fishing, to counter China's efforts in vulnerable Pacific states.
quote: USAID and its allied donors should neutralize these efforts through the deployment of targeted assistance

title: Use Middle East aid to advance the Abraham Accords
proposal: The text recommends focusing Middle East development aid on countries like Morocco and Sudan through joint investments with the UAE and Israel.
quote: USAID should therefore focus its development assistance on countries such as Morocco and Sudan

title: Consider cutting aid to Iraq, Lebanon and the Palestinian territories
proposal: The text recommends USAID consider cutting aid to states allied with Iran, limiting it to narrow priorities such as help for persecuted religious minorities.
quote: USAID should consider cutting aid to states allied to Iran

title: Shrink USAID missions in the Middle East
proposal: The text recommends reducing USAID's mission staff in the Middle East and redirecting funds to lower-cost local partners.
quote: reducing its missions’ footprints in the Middle East

title: Expand Prosper Africa to boost U.S.-Africa business
proposal: The text recommends that USAID and partner agencies use their tools to promote U.S.-African business ties and expand the Prosper Africa initiative.
quote: to facilitate U.S.–African business relationships and expand Prosper Africa

title: Extend AGOA trade preferences for Africa with conditions
proposal: The text recommends extending the African Growth and Opportunity Act beyond 2025 but rewarding good governance and free-market policies.
quote: The next Administration should extend AGOA beyond its 2025 term but within a strategic framework

title: End legacy and underperforming aid programs in Africa
proposal: The text recommends using the 2025 country strategy updates to end legacy and nonperforming programs in Africa and support private-sector growth and diverse energy.
quote: catalyzes private-sector solutions for job creation through increased trade and investment, terminates legacy and

title: Review Latin America aid and end failing programs
proposal: The text recommends reassessing all U.S. aid to Latin America and ending programs that have not produced results, focusing instead on free-market basics.
quote: terminate those that have failed to achieve results after years of effort

title: Fund pro-free-market groups in Latin America
proposal: The text recommends funding private-sector partnerships and civil-society groups, including think tanks, that advocate free-market and democratic ideas, and challenging socialist ideas.
quote: Fund partnerships with the private sector and support civil-society groups, including university centers and think tanks

title: Shift all Latin America aid to local groups by 2030
proposal: The text recommends that USAID commit to moving its entire Latin America portfolio to local organizations by 2030.
quote: the agency should commit to shifting all of its portfolio in the region to local organizations by 2030

title: Halt USAID training on day one and replace it
proposal: The text recommends stopping all agencywide training on the first day and replacing it with training that advances the President's agenda.
quote: On Day One, USAID should halt all agencywide training and replace it with training modules to advance the President’s agenda.

title: Appoint an official to report on USAID policy compliance
proposal: The text recommends a Senior Accountable Official to report on adherence to administration priorities on abortion policy, critical race theory, climate, gender and DEI.
quote: The Administration should appoint a Senior Accountable Official (SAO) to report on the agency’s adherence to Administration policy priorities
